classification.habit: Moderate-sized to large deciduous tree, 15–25 m tall, with a rounded crown.
classification.habitat: Deciduous forests and open dry hill slopes, up to about 1,500 m.
classification.distribution: Throughout India, chiefly in deciduous forests of the sub-Himalayan tract, Central India and the Deccan.

identification.description: Moderate-sized to large deciduous tree with a rounded crown, dark brown cracked bark, ovate leaves bearing a pair of glands at the petiole top, and ovoid five-ribbed yellowish-brown fruits.
identification.whole_plant: Deciduous tree with dark brown longitudinally cracked bark, ovate leaves and yellowish-brown ridged fruits.
identification.stem: Trunk short and cylindrical with spreading branches.
identification.leaf: Simple, alternate or sub-opposite, ovate to elliptic, 7–20 cm long, with a pair of glands at the top of the petiole.
identification.flower: Small, dull white to yellowish, unpleasant-smelling, in terminal spikes.
identification.fruit: Drupe ovoid, 2–3.5 cm long, yellowish-brown, wrinkled and longitudinally five-ribbed when dry; pericarp fibrous, 3–4 mm thick, not adherent to the seed; taste astringent.
identification.seed: Single, hard, pale yellow, bony stone enclosing the kernel.
identification.bark: Dark brown, with longitudinal cracks, exfoliating in woody scales.
identification_points: Ovoid yellowish-brown fruit with five longitudinal ridges
Fibrous pericarp 3–4 mm thick, free from the stone
Pair of glands at the top of the leaf petiole

therapeutics.anupana: Ritu Haritaki: with Saindhava in Varsha, Sharkara in Sharad, Shunthi in Hemanta, Pippali in Shishira, Madhu in Vasanta and Guda in Grishma.
therapeutics.precautions: Laxative in larger doses; may cause loose stools and dehydration. Use carefully in debility, emaciation and after fasting.
therapeutics.contraindications: Classically contraindicated in pregnancy, in persons weakened by travel, fasting, or bloodletting, in emaciation, dehydration and Pitta aggravation with dryness.

shlokas:
हरीतकी पञ्चरसाऽलवणा तुवरा परम्।
रूक्षोष्णा दीपनी मेध्या स्वादुपाका रसायनी॥
चक्षुष्या लघुरायुष्या बृंहणी चानुलोमिनी।

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The pericarp is rich in hydrolysable tannins (chebulinic and chebulagic acids, corilagin) along with gallic acid, ellagic acid and small amounts of anthraquinones.

modern_information.evidence_summary: A key component of Triphala, Haritaki is a powerful rejuvenator and detoxifier, especially for Vata dosha. It supports digestion and colon health.
modern_information.safety_notes: Well tolerated at usual doses; higher doses act as a laxative. Avoid in pregnancy and dehydration.

Seven varieties: Vijaya, Rohini, Putana, Amrita, Abhaya, Jivanti, Chetaki
Formulations: Triphala Churna, Abhayarishta, Agastya Haritaki Rasayana, Chitraka Haritaki
Dose 3–6 g churna; Ritu Haritaki anupana
